summary: Improve source verification, hearing records and legal report writing with hands-on IRAC and CREAC practice. Explore the course and outline.
lede: Court reporting captures hearing events, while legal reporting turns case documents into clear, source-traceable records. For court reporters, legal researchers and case-reporting professionals, this intermediate course develops practical methods for verifying sources, building case chronologies and recording hearings accurately. Learners use IRAC and CREAC to analyze legal issues, summarize judgments and prepare structured reports with careful citations, version control and confidential-information handling.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits professionals who prepare, review or rely on legal case reports, hearing records and supporting source documentation.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working familiarity with legal documents, case files or court proceedings is expected. No coding or programming is required. Exercises use document review, report drafting and basic spreadsheet tracking; advanced information-security and plain-language concepts receive operational introduction rather than implementation-level training.
